question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
solution:
The correct answer is '**benign**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence states that tumours can be of two types, forming a contrast.
 
• The correct pair is “cancerous or benign,” where **benign** means non-cancerous.
 
• This is a standard medical classification: tumours are either malignant (cancerous) or benign (non-cancerous).
 
• Other options do not fit the medical or contextual meaning required here.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Malignant**: Means cancerous, so it cannot pair with “cancerous or …”.
 
• **Benevolent**: Means kind or well-meaning; unrelated to tumours.
 
• **Mild**: Means gentle or not severe; not used as a technical classification for tumours.
